items.statement: For a group Γ acting on a ringed space (X, 𝒪_X): a Γ-equivariant 𝒪_X-module is an 𝒪_X-module ℱ with a homomorphism Γ → Aut(X, ℱ) lifting the action; these form an abelian category with enough injectives (Grothendieck, Tôhoku, Proposition 5.1.1), and Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) ≅ Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)^Γ (Definition A.1). The equivariant cohomology H^i(X, Γ; ℱ) and the equivariant Ext groups Ext^i_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) are the derived functors of ℱ ↦ H^0(X, ℱ)^Γ and of Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, −) (Definition A.2), with spectral sequences H^p(Γ, H^q(X, ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, Γ; ℱ) and H^p(Γ, Ext^q_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_{Γ,𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) (equation (A.1.1)). If π : X → S is Γ-invariant, the R^iπ_*ℱ inherit a Γ-action.

items.name: Equivariant cohomology with supports and the localization sequence
items.statement: For a Γ-stable closed D ⊂ X with complement j : U → X, 0 → j_!𝒪_U → 𝒪_X → i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X → 0 identifies Hom_{𝒪_X}(i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X, ℱ) with the sections Γ_D(X, ℱ) supported in D; H^i_D(X, Γ; ℱ) are the derived functors of ℱ ↦ Γ_D(X, ℱ)^Γ = Hom_{Γ,𝒪_X}(i_*i^{-1}𝒪_X, ℱ) (Definition A.3). There is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i_D(X, Γ; ℱ) → H^i(X, Γ; ℱ) → H^i(U, Γ; ℱ) → H^{i+1}_D(X, Γ; ℱ) → ⋯ and a spectral sequence H^p(Γ, H^q_D(X, ℱ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_D(X, Γ; ℱ).

items.name: Derived limits in a triangulated category
items.statement: K is a derived limit R lim K_n of an inverse system (K_n, f_n) in a triangulated category 𝒟 if ∏K_n exists and there is a distinguished triangle K → ∏K_n → ∏K_n → K[1], the middle map being (k_n) ↦ (k_n − f_{n+1}(k_{n+1})); it is unique up to non-unique isomorphism (Definition B.1). For every L there is an exact sequence 0 → R^1 lim Hom(L, K_n[−1]) → Hom(L, R lim K_n) → lim Hom(L, K_n) → 0 (Lemma B.2; Stacks, Tag 0919).

items.name: Galois gerb with algebraic kernel
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero Galois extension k′/k, a gerb is a topological extension 1→H(k′)→Q→Gal(k′/k)→1, with discrete kernel, algebraic semilinear conjugation, and a continuous section over a finite-index Galois subgroup giving the required descent and semidirect-product chart.

items.name: Morphisms and conjugacy of Galois gerbs
items.statement: A gerb morphism is continuous over the Galois group and algebraic on the kernel. Conjugacy is by target-kernel points. For pro-gerbs keep the compatible finite-stage conjugacy data.

items.name: Gerb isomorphism scheme and automorphism group
items.statement: For morphisms f1,f2 into the neutral gerb of G, the functor of kernel-point conjugators is the descended k-scheme Isom(f1,f2); I_f=Isom(f,f) is its automorphism group.

items.name: Crossed module and quotient groupoid
items.statement: A homomorphism ∂:F→H with H-action on F satisfies equivariance and the Peiffer identity. Its quotient groupoid H/F has objects H and arrows f:h1→h2 when h2=∂(f)h1, with the induced strict monoidal structure.

items.name: Monoidal isomorphism and conjugacy data
items.statement: For strict monoidal functors, retain natural isomorphisms respecting tensor and unit, conjugacy by a target group element, and the composite relation conjugate-isomorphism.

items.name: Simply connected quotient as a Picard groupoid
items.statement: For connected reductive G over characteristic zero, the canonical G-action on Gsc from the lifted commutator gives Gsc→G a crossed module and the quotient G/Gsc a Picard groupoid; retain its neutral-gerb analogue.

items.name: Two-fiber product of categories
items.statement: For F1:C1→C and F2:C2→C, objects are (c1,c2,α:F1(c1)≃F2(c2)); arrows are pairs making the comparison square commute. Strict monoidal structures induce the compatible monoidal two-fiber product.

items.name: Semidirect quotient for compatible actions
items.statement: If Δ acts on H and Γ⊂H, with equivariant Γ→Δ acting by conjugation on H, define H*ΓΔ=(H⋊Δ)/{(γ,φ(γ)^−1)}. This is the source’s semidirect quotient, not an arbitrary free amalgamated product.

items.name: Twist of a representation by a torsor
items.statement: For an affine Q-group Z, right Z-torsor P and Q-representation W, define W^P=(W⊗Q O(P))^Z using (zf)(x)=f(xz) on functions and the diagonal action.

items.name: Module twist by an affine torsor
items.statement: For flat affine Z/A, a Z-torsor P and an A-module M with Z-action, define the twist as (M⊗_A O_P)^Z.

items.name: Spread of a pointed good compactification
items.statement: For the chosen (X_F,Xbar_F,D_F,xbar), after inverting an integer N>0, spread the smooth projective compactification, relative SNC divisor and algebraic geometric basepoint to O_F[1/N], with geometrically connected fibres and xbar integral over Zbar[1/N].

items.name: Weil restriction of scalars
items.statement: For a finite étale extension of rings and a scheme over the larger ring, the Weil restriction represents the functor of points over the smaller ring, giving a canonical bijection on integral points.

items.name: Sections of a module over a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I = (f₁,…,f_r) ⊂ A, U = Spec A \ V(I), and M an A-module. Define Sec_U(M) := Γ(U, M̃). By the sheaf axiom for the cover U = ∪_i D(f_i), Sec_U(M) is the kernel of ∏_i M_{f_i} → ∏_{i<j} M_{f_if_j}, (m_i)_i ↦ (m_i − m_j)_{i<j} (images in M_{f_if_j}). For r = 0 (U = ∅), Sec_U(M) = 0.

items.name: Hartogs closure H_U(J) of an ideal
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring and U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open such that the restriction A → Γ(U, 𝒪_U) is an isomorphism. For an ideal J ⊂ A, H_U(J) is the image of Γ(U, J̃|_U) ↪ Γ(U, 𝒪_U) ≅ A; it is an ideal of A containing J. The embedding into A (not only the isomorphism class of Γ(U, J̃|_U)) is part of the construction.

items.name: Artinian formal etaleness at a point
items.statement: A morphism of functors on Noetherian rings is formally etale at x:Spec k->F in this section if every compatible Artinian local thickening Spec A->G with residue field k admits a unique lift to F. For representable locally finite-type morphisms with locally Noetherian target this implies etaleness; it is deliberately weaker than the unrestricted formal-lifting definition.

items.name: Unibranch points and normalization
items.statement: A point y is unibranch when the normalization of the reduced local ring is local. Under finite normalization its fibre is then a single point, equivalently connected. For a REDUCED excellent Noetherian local ring, unibranchness is equivalent to its completion being a domain. The printed remark omits reducedness (source issue E9); dual numbers show why it is necessary.

items.name: Analytically unramified formal stack
items.statement: A topologically finite type p-adic formal algebraic stack is analytically unramified when all smooth affine charts have reduced rings, equivalently its finite-type versal rings are reduced. Its associated reduced formal stack pulls back to Spf A_red. Distinguish this from the underlying reduced algebraic stack Spec(A/I)_red.

items.name: Cycle of a finite module
items.statement: For a finite module on a type's special-fiber versal ring, its top-dimensional cycle sums each irreducible component with coefficient equal to the length of the module localized at its generic prime.

items.name: Elkik's presentation-dependent Jacobian ideal
items.statement: For B=A[X_1,…,X_N]/J with fixed generators f_1,…,f_q, for each subset α of the generators let F_α be their ideal, Δ_α the ideal of |α|×|α| minors of their Jacobian (zero if |α|>N), and K_α=(F_α:J). Put H=Σ_α K_αΔ_α, with the usual empty-minor convention. Elkik permits a chosen H_B⊂H. The vanishing locus of the image of H in B is the nonsmooth locus.

items.name: Maximal-ideal associated graded algebra
items.statement: For a commutative local ring (R,m,k), construct gr_m(R)=⊕_{n≥0} m^n/m^(n+1) as an N-graded commutative k-algebra. Scalar multiplication uses R→k since m annihilates each quotient; multiplication sends the classes of a∈m^i,b∈m^j to ab modulo m^(i+j+1). No choice of a coefficient-field section k→R is required.

items.name: Chow operations and Chern classes
items.statement: Use Chow groups with proper pushforward, flat and refined lci pullback, Chern classes and intersection products, with explicit cycle multiplicities and rational coefficients where required.

items.name: Perfection of an algebraic space
items.statement: For a characteristic-p algebraic space Y0, Y0^perf is the inverse limit along absolute Frobenius, with its projection to Y0; a perfect space has invertible Frobenius. Work over a perfect field k.

items.name: Perfect finite presentation and deperfections
items.statement: A perfect k-algebraic space Y is pfp when Y≃Y0^perf for some finitely presented k-algebraic space Y0. A deperfection is such Y0 together with the comparison.

items.name: Perfect properness
items.statement: A morphism of pfp perfect spaces is perfectly proper when it is the perfection of a proper finite-presentation morphism. Use the source exact equivalence with its valuative/topological formulation.

items.name: Perfect smoothness with relative dimension
items.statement: A map f:Y→Z of perfect k-spaces is perfectly smooth of dimension d at y if étale neighborhoods admit a factorization U→(A^d)^perf×V→V with first map étale; d is nonnegative.

items.name: Weak perfect smoothness
items.statement: f:Y→Z is weakly perfectly smooth of relative dimension d at y when an open neighborhood U of y admits a surjective perfectly smooth g:X→U of dimension e and f∘g is perfectly smooth of dimension e+d. The unqualified property admits such covers locally.

items.name: Perfect algebraic stacks
items.statement: A pfp perfect algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids on perfect k-schemes with representable pfp diagonal and a representable surjective perfectly smooth atlas by a pfp perfect algebraic space, with the source diagonal conventions.

items.name: Weak smooth maps of perfect stacks
items.statement: For a map of perfect stacks, test weak perfect smoothness on smooth atlases using the source convention; a map may be nonrepresentable. Track atlas dimensions when defining the stack relative dimension.

items.name: Contraction
items.statement: A scheme or algebraic-space morphism f:X→Y is a contraction when proper and surjective and the canonical O_Y→f_*O_X is an isomorphism. Universal validity after every base change is a stronger condition, not part of this definition.

items.name: Characteristic-zero fiber
items.statement: For a scheme or algebraic space X, X_Q is X×Spec(Z)Spec(Q), with its projection; likewise X_Fp. These are base changes, not a choice of one generic point.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic scheme
items.statement: A connected scheme X is mixed-characteristic in the paper's convention when X_Q is nonempty and X_Fp is nonempty for some prime p.

items.name: Universal homeomorphism
items.statement: A morphism is a universal homeomorphism when every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces. For algebraic spaces, representability is an additional hypothesis and is not automatic.

items.name: Elementary subintegral extension
items.statement: An inclusion A⊆B is elementary if B=A[b] for b with b²,b³∈A.

items.name: Relative spectrum
items.statement: For a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra A, Spec_X A represents maps to X equipped with an algebra homomorphism A→f_*O.

items.name: Finite set-theoretic equivalence relation
items.statement: For X separated finite type over Noetherian S, σ₁,σ₂:E⇒X are finite and E→X×S X is injective on points valued in every algebraically closed field, with equivalence-relation image. Nilpotents in E are allowed; the map need not be a monomorphism.

items.name: Geometric quotient of a finite relation
items.statement: A categorical coequalizer X→Y in separated finite-type S-algebraic spaces is geometric if finite and its geometric-point fibers are exactly the equivalence classes.

items.name: Proper group action
items.statement: For an affine group scheme G of finite type over Noetherian S acting on X, properness means (m,p₂):G×S X→X×S X is proper.

items.name: Topological quotient of a proper action
items.statement: A G-invariant map q:X→Z is a topological quotient if locally of finite type, universally submersive, and induces the orbit-space bijection on all algebraically closed-field points.

items.name: Geometric quotient of a proper action
items.statement: A topological quotient is geometric if O_Z→(q_*O_X)^G is an isomorphism.

items.name: Topological pushout datum
items.statement: Given Y→pX and Y→gY′ with p representable quasi-compact quasi-separated and g representable universal homeomorphism, a topological pushout is a commuting square with X→fX′ representable universal homeomorphism. The terminology alone does not assert a categorical pushout.

items.name: Geometric pushout
items.statement: A topological pushout is geometric if O_X′→f_*O_X ×_(fp)_*O_Y q_*O_Y′ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.

items.name: Conductor square for a finite reduced surjection
items.statement: For finite surjective f:Y→X of reduced Noetherian schemes, define the conductor I locally as {s∈B:sB⊆A} for A⊆B. It is an ideal in both rings and A=B×_(B/I)(A/I); this does not require birationality.

items.name: Direct-limit multiplicative perfection
items.statement: For a commutative monoid M and prime p, M^perf is the filtered colimit M→M→… of p-th powers. Applied to a Z_(p)-algebra this forgets addition; p-th power is not a mixed-characteristic ring map.

items.name: Perfection of a line-bundle sheaf
items.statement: For L on a Z_(p)-scheme, L^perf is the sheafification of the set-presheaf colimit of L^(p^n) under p-th powers of sections. Define H⁰(X,L)^perf as the analogous colimit of global-section sets.

items.name: Picard groupoid
items.statement: Pic(X) has line bundles as objects and only isomorphisms as morphisms. It is the core of the existing full invertible-sheaf category, not the Picard group of isomorphism classes.

items.name: Picard groupoid with formal p-power roots
items.statement: Pic(X)[1/p] has objects (L,n), n∈N, and Hom((L,n),(M,m))=colim_(N≥n,m) Isom(L^(p^(N−n)),M^(p^(N−m))).

items.name: Relative spectrum in Stein factorization
items.statement: For a proper map f:X→Y of algebraic spaces, form Y′=Spec_Y(f_*O_X). It factors f as h:X→Y′ then π:Y′→Y, with h proper and surjective, π integral, and O_Y′≅h_*O_X canonically. Formation commutes with flat base change.

items.name: Shared integral Chow and refined-intersection supplier
items.statement: For finite-type schemes over a field, import integral Chow groups formed from L09, proper pushforward with residue-degree weights, flat and lci pullback, refined Gysin for regular immersions, Chern operators, the Whitney formula, zero-section self-intersection and excess/projection formulas. These are the existing SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 targets; this paper supplies applications, not a second theory. Keep Gysin operations with singular base changes distinct from a purity isomorphism for singular schemes.

items.name: Localized Chern classes with a rank threshold
items.statement: Let X be finite type over a field, Z⊂X closed, and K a bounded complex of finite-rank locally free O_X-modules. Suppose K|U, U=X−Z, has cohomology only in degree zero and H0(K)|U is locally free of rank n−1, n≥1. Bloch’s construction supplies c_i^X_Z(K) in bivariant CH^i(Z→X) for i≥n; lower-degree classes remain ordinary Chern classes on X. In particular K need not be acyclic on U. Retain the global-image, quasi-isomorphism, support-enlargement and proper-pushforward properties below as explicit construction obligations.

items.name: §A.1 (rational Chow groups of proper cycles on Deligne–Mumford stacks)
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack X locally of finite type over k, Ch_{c,i}(X)_Q is the colimit of Ch_i(Y)_Q over closed substacks Y ⊆ X proper over k (§A.1.2); the degree map satisfies deg([x]) = [k_x : k]/|Aut(x)|_{k_x} (§A.1.3); for X smooth separated of pure dimension n the refined Gysin map along the diagonal gives the intersection product Ch_{c,i} × Ch_{c,j} → Ch_{c,i+j−n} and the pairing ⟨ , ⟩_X (A.1) (§A.1.4); the cycle class map cl_X : Ch_{c,j}(X)_Q → H^{2n−2j}_c(X ⊗_k k̄, Q_ℓ)(n−j) intertwines it with the cup product (§A.1.5); and cCh_n(X × X)_Q, the colimit over correspondences Z with proper first projection, is an associative Q-algebra acting on Ch_{c,i}(X)_Q (§A.1.6).

items.name: Chow groups of Artin stacks, refined Gysin maps and Riemann–Roch
items.statement: Chow groups of algebraic stacks with proper pushforward and flat pullback, refined Gysin maps for regular local immersions and for morphisms with vector bundle normal cone stacks, the excess intersection formula, deformation to the normal cone, and the Riemann–Roch map τ_X relating K-theory and Chow groups.

items.name: Chow operations for the cycle construction
items.statement: Use rational equivalence, proper pushforward with residue multiplicities, flat/lci pullback, Chern classes and projection/excess-intersection formulas on the actual schemes/stacks in the moduli problem; a finite unramified divisor map need not be a closed immersion.

items.name: Fpqc space
items.statement: Over a field k, a k-space is a set-valued fpqc sheaf on affine k-schemes: finite disjoint unions map to products and faithfully flat ring maps give the usual equalizer.

items.name: Algebraic space and representable morphism
items.statement: An algebraic space is an étale sheaf with schematic diagonal and an étale surjective scheme atlas. Quasi-separatedness is not imposed here. A map of spaces is representable if its affine-test pullbacks are algebraic spaces.

items.name: Perfect algebraic space
items.statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, a perfect algebraic space has invertible absolute Frobenius. Relative Frobenius and the Frobenius-twisted k-structure are used for k-linear maps.

items.name: Perfection functor
items.statement: Perfection X^perf is the inverse Frobenius limit, interpreted with k-twists. It is right adjoint to inclusion of perfect algebraic spaces; on affine rings it is the direct-limit perfect closure.

items.name: Affine-group torsor and contracted product
items.statement: For an affine group H, an H-torsor E→X is fpqc and satisfies E×H≅E×_X E. For an H-space T define E×^H T as the fpqc quotient of E×T by the diagonal action.

items.name: Perfect-site space and ind-perfect algebraic space
items.statement: A perfect k-space is an fpqc sheaf on perfect affine k-schemes. An ind-perfect algebraic space is such a sheaf presented by a filtered union of perfect algebraic spaces with closed transition maps.

items.name: Perfect finite-presentation conditions
items.statement: Locally perfectly finite type means an étale affine atlas by perfections of finite-type k-affines. Perfectly finite type adds quasi-compactness; pfp adds quasi-separatedness. A model is a finite-presentation algebraic space X′ with X≅(X′)^perf.

items.name: Weakly normal model with prescribed generic fields
items.statement: For pfp perfect X, choose finitely generated k-subfields K_i of each generic residue field whose perfections give that field. The corresponding weakly normal finite-presentation model is unique with these identifications.

items.name: Perfectly proper morphism
items.statement: A morphism of pfp perfect algebraic spaces is perfectly proper if separated and universally closed.

items.name: Perfect smoothness
items.statement: A map f:X→Y of pfp perfect algebraic spaces is perfectly smooth at x if étale charts factor it as an étale map to V×(A^n)^perf followed by projection.

items.name: The Bégueri resolution
items.statement: For a commutative, finite, locally free group G over a scheme S with Cartier dual G^*, there is a short exact sequence 0 → G → Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) → Q → 0 of fppf sheaves with Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) and Q commutative, smooth, affine S-group schemes; the map Res_{G^*/S}(𝔾_m) → Q is faithfully flat and finitely presented, so the sequence stays exact on the fppf site of any animated algebra over S.

items.name: Syntomic, ind-fppf and ind-syntomic ring maps
items.statement: A ring map A → A' is syntomic if Spec(A') is covered by spectra of A-algebras A[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) with each A[x]/(f_1, …, f_i) flat over A and f_1, …, f_c regular in A[x]_𝔭 for primes 𝔭 ⊇ (f); it is ind-fppf (resp. ind-syntomic) if A' is a filtered colimit of faithfully flat, finitely presented (resp. syntomic) A-algebras, equivalently if every A-map B → A' from a finitely presented B factors through a faithfully flat finitely presented (resp. syntomic) A-algebra. These classes are stable under composition, base change, finite products and filtered colimits; A → Â for a Noetherian local Q-algebra with a nonreduced formal fibre is flat but not ind-fppf.

items.name: The pro-fppf site
items.statement: A scheme map X' → X is pro-ppf (resp. pro-fppf) if X' is covered by affine opens Spec(A') mapping to affine opens Spec(A) ⊂ X with A' a filtered colimit of flat, finitely presented A-algebras (resp. and X' → X faithfully flat); pro-ppf families form a pro-fppf cover if every quasi-compact open is a finite union of images of quasi-compact opens. Pro-fppf covers are fpqc covers.

items.name: Flat, faithfully flat and étale maps of animated rings
items.statement: An animated A-module M is flat (resp. faithfully flat) if π_0(M) is so over π_0(A) and π_*(A) ⊗_{π_0 A} π_0(M) ≅ π_*(M); then π_*(M' ⊗^L_A M) ≅ π_*(M') ⊗_{π_0 A} π_0(M) for every animated M'. A map of animated rings is flat, faithfully flat, étale, finitely presented or finite if A' is flat and π_0(f) has the property; fpqc, fppf and étale covers define Grothendieck topologies on animated rings and give no new covers of 0-truncated rings.

items.name: Étale and fppf cohomology over an animated ring
items.statement: For an animated ring A, étale, fppf and fpqc sheaves (the last with a cardinal bound) are ∞-sheaves on flat A-algebras; RΓ_ét(A, F) and RΓ_fppf(A, F) are the values of sheafifications, and RΓ_fppf(U_A, F) = R lim RΓ_fppf(A', F) over fppf A' factoring through an open U ⊂ Spec(π_0 A). For 0-truncated A this is classical cohomology; for a commutative affine R-group G, G(A) ≅ τ^{≤0} RΓ_fppf(A, G), so cohomology may be nonzero in negative degrees; quasi-coherent sheaves are hypersheaves.

items.name: The Brauer group of a scheme
items.statement: For a scheme X, Br(X) = ∪_{n>0} im(H^1(X, PGL_n) → H^2(X, 𝔾_m)_tors), the classes of Azumaya algebras.

items.name: Resolution of cyclic quotient surface singularities
items.statement: The minimal resolution of a complex surface singularity of type 1/n(1,a), with gcd(a,n)=1 and 0<a<n, replaces it by a chain of smooth rational curves with intersection matrix determined by the negative continued fraction n/a.

items.name: Character sheaves on an abelian variety (Definitions 2.3, 2.4)
items.statement: For a continuous character χ : π₁^et(A_k‾) → ℚ‾_p^×, L_χ is the unique rank-one sheaf on A_k‾ with monodromy χ. If χ is Gal(k‾|k)-invariant, L_χ denotes the unique lisse rank-one sheaf on A_k whose associated representation restricts to χ and whose stalk at the identity has trivial Galois action, obtained from the splitting of 1 → π₁^et(A_k‾) → π₁^et(A_k) → Gal(k‾|k) → 1 given by the identity section. For such χ, P^χ is the subcategory of perverse K with H^i(A_k‾, Q ⊗ L_χ) = 0 for i ≠ 0 and all subquotients Q of K_k‾, and N^χ := P^χ ∩ N.

items.name: Free groups, characters of the fundamental group and the dual torus
items.statement: The character group Π(A) of the étale fundamental group of an abelian variety, a torus over ℚ‾_p whose torsion points are the finite-order characters; torsion translates of proper subtori are the loci to be avoided.
